Event type set: exhaustive match confirmed against types.ts's AssistantMessageEvent discriminated union (start/text_start/text_delta/text_end/thinking_start/thinking_delta/thinking_end/toolcall_start/toolcall_delta/toolcall_end/done/error) -- identical variant set both sides, no divergence. Error/end semantics: is_terminal()==Done|Error matches TS's isComplete (event.type==="done"||"error"); result()/extractResult message-extraction logic (Done->message, Error->error) matches. Abort: event_stream.rs itself has zero abort-specific logic on either side -- abort is handled entirely at the provider level via AbortSignal checks, out of this unit's scope. ONE divergence found, NOT applied (verdict=none): oracle's push() (event_stream.rs:32-46) only gates the ONE-SHOT final-result oneshot against a second terminal event via `Option::take()` -- it still unconditionally forwards every event (including ones pushed after a terminal event) to the mpsc receiver. TS's push() has a `if (this.done) return;` guard at the top that silently drops ALL events (delivery included, not just the already-resolved final-result) once a terminal event has been seen. Not applied because: (a) unreachable in practice -- grepped every `stream.push(` call site across src/providers/*.ts and register-builtins.ts; every single one pushes exactly one terminal event immediately followed by `.end()`, with zero further pushes after; (b) plausibly an artifact of how oracle had to split sender/receiver across an mpsc channel + a separate oneshot (Rust ownership forces this split; the mpsc side has no reason to duplicate the oneshot's one-shot guard) rather than a deliberate behavioral choice -- oracle's own header frames this file as modeling the pre-existing TS design, not the other way around, unlike most other units in this migration; (c) TS's guard is a defensible safety net (protects a consumer's already-terminated iteration from a buggy double-push) with no downside for any current caller. Changing this shared low-level plumbing (used by all 20+ provider files) for a zero-practical-benefit edge case was judged disproportionate risk; flagged here per the meta-rule instead of decided unilaterally. Locked with a test asserting the CURRENT (unchanged) drop behavior so a future change is a deliberate, reviewed decision.
